societies.name: Classical Athens
societies.summary: Athenian civic institutions and imperial alliances coexisted with slavery and restricted citizenship.

societies.name: Sparta / Lacedaemon
societies.summary: Military-oriented polis with dependent helot labour and shifting Greek alliances.

societies.name: Thebes and the Boeotian leagues
societies.summary: Competing regional power in mainland Greek politics.

societies.name: Delian League / Athenian maritime empire
societies.summary: Greek naval alliance increasingly directed by Athens.

societies.name: Kingdom of Macedon
societies.summary: Macedonian monarchy expanded under Philip II and Alexander III.

societies.name: Kingdom of Epirus
societies.summary: Greek-speaking kingdom linked to western Balkan and Italian campaigns.

societies.name: Achaean League
societies.summary: Federal polity incorporating multiple Greek communities before Roman conquest.

societies.name: Aetolian League
societies.summary: Regional federation and rival of Macedonian and Achaean interests.

societies.name: Etruscan city-states
societies.summary: Urban cultures of central Italy with varied city governments; not a single empire.

societies.name: Roman Republic
societies.summary: Roman magistracies and senate oversaw Mediterranean conquest while institutions changed through civil war.

societies.name: Roman Empire / imperial Principate
societies.summary: The imperial Roman system expanded and changed administrative form; later East and West had distinct courts.

societies.name: Western Roman imperial court
societies.summary: Western imperial office traditionally terminated in 476; provincial populations and institutions continued.

societies.name: Eastern Roman imperial government
societies.summary: Eastern Roman imperial administration persisted beyond the western imperial office.

societies.name: Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy
societies.summary: Theoderic established a post-western-imperial kingdom alongside surviving Roman institutions.

societies.name: Gothic and Visigothic polities
societies.summary: Gothic military and settlement formations changed under and after Roman authority.

societies.name: Early Frankish confederations
societies.summary: Frankish-speaking regional coalitions and emerging kingship in late Roman Gaul.

societies.name: Vandal Kingdom in North Africa
societies.summary: Political rule over former Roman African territories; African communities persisted.

societies.name: Carthaginian / Punic polity
societies.summary: Commercial and military power of the western Mediterranean until Roman destruction of its capital.

societies.name: Numidian kingdoms
societies.summary: Berber-speaking political formations; Masinissa fostered royal urban and agricultural institutions.

societies.name: Kingdom of Mauretania
societies.summary: Client kingship of Juba II and successors preceding direct Roman annexation.

societies.name: Amazigh/Berber regional communities
societies.summary: Diverse local populations whose continuity cannot be reduced to Punic or Roman administrations.

societies.name: Kingdom of Kush / Meroitic Nubia
societies.summary: Nile kingdom with royal cemeteries and distinctive Meroitic writing, religious and craft traditions.

societies.name: Late Period Egypt and Persian periods
societies.summary: Persian domination occurred in several episodes amid local Egyptian dynastic politics.

societies.name: Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt
societies.summary: Hellenistic dynasty in Egypt from Alexander-era successors until Roman annexation.

societies.name: Roman provincial Egypt
societies.summary: Roman governorship and grain economy retained Egyptian and Greek cultural diversity.

societies.name: Aksumite Kingdom
societies.summary: Red Sea power with coinage, long-distance trade, stelae and fourth-century royal Christian conversion.

societies.name: Adulis Red Sea port community
societies.summary: Commercial port associated with Aksum and maritime connections to Arabia and the Indian Ocean.

societies.name: Garamantian oasis settlements
societies.summary: Saharan oasis civilisation with irrigation and caravan networks; dates are broad.

societies.name: Nok archaeological traditions
societies.summary: Iron-working and terracotta traditions from disparate archaeological communities; not a single kingdom.

societies.name: Jenne-jeno early urban settlement
societies.summary: Archaeological urban settlement tradition without a contemporary royal chronology.

societies.name: Central African iron-age farming communities
societies.summary: Diverse iron-using agrarian communities; no unity of government should be presumed.

societies.name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
societies.summary: Imperial administration linked diverse satrapies and roads; exact frontiers fluctuated.

societies.name: Seleucid Empire
societies.summary: Hellenistic imperial succession with changing domains across the Near East.

societies.name: Parthian / Arsacid Empire
societies.summary: Arsacid political networks mediated east-west exchange and rivalled Rome.

societies.name: Sasanian Empire
societies.summary: Persian imperial dynasty succeeding the Arsacids; continued into 500-1000 batch.

societies.name: Artaxiad Kingdom of Armenia
societies.summary: Regional kingdom contested by Roman and Parthian expansion.

societies.name: Arsacid Armenia
societies.summary: Armenian kingship engaged with Roman and Sasanian powers; fourth-century conversion tradition.

societies.name: Nabataean Kingdom
societies.summary: Caravan-linked kingdom annexed as Roman Arabia in 106 CE.

societies.name: Hasmonean Kingdom of Judaea
societies.summary: Jewish political dynasty arising after the Maccabean revolts.

societies.name: Herodian client kingdoms
societies.summary: Roman-linked Judean monarchy and successors; boundaries and jurisdictions varied.

societies.name: Palmyrene city and kingdom
societies.summary: Oasis city of trans-regional trade, later briefly centre of a breakaway Roman-era kingdom.

societies.name: Kingdom of Osrhoene / Edessa
societies.summary: Local kingdom and commercial centre between Roman and Parthian spheres.

societies.name: Hatra city-state
societies.summary: Fortified religious and mercantile centre in an imperial contact zone.

societies.name: Kingdom of Saba
societies.summary: South Arabian state and irrigation landscapes tied to incense exchange.

societies.name: Kingdom of Maʿin
societies.summary: Commercial South Arabian kingdom in long-distance incense networks.

societies.name: Kingdom of Qataban
societies.summary: South Arabian polity interacting with Saba and other neighbouring kingdoms.

societies.name: Kingdom of Hadramaut
societies.summary: South Arabian kingdom connected to aromatic-resin trade.

societies.name: Himyarite Kingdom
societies.summary: South Arabian power that reconfigured earlier kingdoms and continued beyond 500 CE.

societies.name: Greco-Bactrian Kingdom
societies.summary: Hellenistic kingdom connecting Greek and Central Asian political worlds.

societies.name: Indo-Greek kingdoms
societies.summary: Successor Hellenistic polities with distinctive numismatic and cultural repertoires.

societies.name: Sogdian oasis city networks
societies.summary: Urban oasis networks interacting with steppe powers and cross-continental commerce.

societies.name: Saka and Scythian-related steppe communities
societies.summary: Distinct communities grouped under external ethnonyms; avoid one polity or fixed border.

societies.name: Sarmatian groupings
societies.summary: Pastoral confederacies with changing group identities and Roman frontier relationships.

societies.name: Xiongnu confederation
societies.summary: Major steppe polity in sustained diplomatic and military interaction with Han states.

societies.name: Yuezhi / emerging Kushan confederations
societies.summary: Migration and political restructuring preceding Kushan imperial dominance.

societies.name: Kingdom of Khotan
societies.summary: Oasis polity in trans-Asian networks; early chronology largely conventional.

societies.name: Kucha oasis polity
societies.summary: Oasis society with later prominent Buddhist textual heritage; early formation uncertain.

societies.name: Maurya Empire
societies.summary: Imperial polity associated with Ashoka and surviving inscriptions.

societies.name: Magadha kingdoms
societies.summary: Regional states that formed the institutional base for the Nanda and Maurya empires.

societies.name: Nanda dynasty
societies.summary: Late pre-Mauryan ruling house; conventional regnal dates vary in sources.

societies.name: Shunga dynasty
societies.summary: Post-Mauryan ruling dynasty alongside other regional polities.

societies.name: Kanva dynasty
societies.summary: Short-lived successor in Magadhan dynastic narratives.

societies.name: Kushan Empire
societies.summary: Transregional power tied to Central Asian, Iranian and South Asian religious and economic history.

societies.name: Indo-Scythian / Shaka kingdoms
societies.summary: Successor and overlapping regional powers; not one single dynasty over the whole interval.

societies.name: Western Kshatrapas
societies.summary: Shaka-linked regional ruling houses with extensive coinage and inscriptions.

societies.name: Satavahana dynasty
societies.summary: Regional rule and long-distance exchange linked to western Indian Ocean ports.

societies.name: Ikshvaku dynasty of Andhra
societies.summary: Post-Satavahana patronage and religious architecture in southeastern Deccan.

societies.name: Vakataka dynasty
societies.summary: Regional kingdom closely associated with fifth-century artistic patronage.

societies.name: Gupta Empire
societies.summary: Major political formation supporting Sanskrit literary, mathematical, scientific and religious scholarship.

societies.name: Anuradhapura kingdoms / period
societies.summary: Long-lived Sri Lankan political and Buddhist institutions with changing dynasties.

societies.name: Early Chera polities
societies.summary: Tamil-speaking western coastal polities associated with maritime and inland commerce.

societies.name: Early Chola polities
societies.summary: Early Tamil political tradition; separate from much later imperial Chola dynasty.

societies.name: Early Pandya polities
societies.summary: Tamil-language political formation and exchange connections; early chronology approximate.

societies.name: Early Pallava polities
societies.summary: Emerging regional power before major seventh-century royal architecture.

societies.name: Eastern Zhou royal houses
societies.summary: Zhou royal continuity amid competing regional states.

societies.name: Warring States Chinese polities
societies.summary: Multiple independent states with warfare, philosophies, bureaucracy and technological development.

societies.name: Qin Empire
societies.summary: Short-lived unification with standardising imperial reforms.

societies.name: Han dynasty / imperial administration
societies.summary: Western and Eastern Han administrations separated by Xin interregnum; retain time-sliced detail.

societies.name: Western Han dynasty
societies.summary: Early Han court and political institutions before Wang Mang.

societies.name: Xin dynasty under Wang Mang
societies.summary: Short-lived dynastic interregnum with controversial reform programmes.

societies.name: Eastern Han dynasty
societies.summary: Later Han phase preceding Three Kingdoms division.

societies.name: Cao Wei
societies.summary: One of the Three Kingdoms after the Han political collapse.

societies.name: Shu Han
societies.summary: Southwestern Three Kingdoms polity.

societies.name: Eastern Wu
societies.summary: Lower Yangtze polity in Three Kingdoms era.

societies.name: Western Jin
societies.summary: Partial reunification of China after Three Kingdoms.

societies.name: Eastern Jin
societies.summary: Southern court with influential literati culture.

societies.name: Northern Wei
societies.summary: Xianbei-founded northern dynasty with cave-temple patronage and changing administrative traditions.

societies.name: Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties
societies.summary: Southern Chinese dynasty distinct from 10th-century Song.

societies.name: Southern Qi dynasty
societies.summary: Shorter-lived southern dynasty at the fifth-century boundary.

societies.name: Baekje kingdom
societies.summary: Traditional foundation date is not independently secured; archaeological state formation gradual.

societies.name: Goguryeo kingdom
societies.summary: Powerful Korean polity that eliminated Lelang in 313; traditional founding date uncertain.

societies.name: Silla kingdom
societies.summary: Korean kingdom with royal tombs, artisan traditions and later consolidation; early foundation traditional.

societies.name: Gaya confederation
societies.summary: Confederated communities noted for elite iron and ceramic cultures.

societies.name: Yayoi-period Japanese communities
societies.summary: Wet-rice agriculture and regional political differentiation; cultural-period label not polity.

societies.name: Kofun-era Yamato political networks
societies.summary: Elite mounded burials and gradually enlarging political integration; early royal chronologies unreliable.

societies.name: Dong Son bronze-drum tradition
societies.summary: Regional metalworking and ritual drums traded over mainland and island Southeast Asia.

societies.name: Sa Huynh cultural traditions
societies.summary: Jar burials, imported beads and connections to island Southeast Asia.

societies.name: Oc Eo maritime settlement networks
societies.summary: Canal-linked settlements with Indian Ocean and South China Sea commerce.

societies.name: Funan-labelled lower Mekong polities
societies.summary: Collective name in Chinese textual accounts; cannot be given a precise modern-style territorial polygon.

societies.name: Linyi and early Champa-related polities
societies.summary: Coastal and inland political formations known partly through Chinese records.

societies.name: Ban Chiang regional Bronze-Iron traditions
societies.summary: Long duration pottery, burial and metal traditions; dating varies substantially by phase.

societies.name: Plain of Jars related regional sites
societies.summary: Megalithic jar tradition with uncertain precise period mapping.

societies.name: Sembiran and north Bali trading settlements
societies.summary: Indian ceramics and scripts occur in an island Southeast Asian exchange context.

societies.name: Early Pyu urban traditions
societies.summary: Early urban settlement tradition on mainland Southeast Asia; avoid precise first-city dates.

societies.name: Late Olmec cultural centres
societies.summary: Regional material and ceremonial traditions with decline of La Venta near the 500 BCE boundary.

societies.name: Epi-Olmec Gulf Coast cultures
societies.summary: Distinct late Formative art and script communities following Olmec period.

societies.name: Cuicuilco settlement
societies.summary: Formative urban ceremonial centre impacted by volcanism and changing settlement patterns.

societies.name: Teotihuacan urban polity
societies.summary: Large monumental and residential city with influence across Mesoamerica.

societies.name: Monte Alban / Zapotec urban state
societies.summary: Hilltop civic-ceremonial and political centre with different construction phases.

societies.name: Teuchitlan tradition communities
societies.summary: Western Mexican civic and ritual traditions with circular complexes.

societies.name: Western Mexican shaft-tomb traditions
societies.summary: Burial customs and ceramic regional styles; not a single bounded polity.

societies.name: Regional Veracruz cultures
societies.summary: Regional artistic and ritual cultures beyond the early Olmec sequence.

societies.name: Maya lowland Preclassic communities
societies.summary: Town and ceremonial networks before Classic-era dynastic inscriptions.

societies.name: Maya cultural region (Classic-era city states)
societies.summary: Cultural and writing traditions across politically independent city-states; not a unified empire.

societies.name: Tikal Maya polity
societies.summary: Major city with preclassic occupation and Classic-period dynastic political record.

societies.name: Copan Maya polity
societies.summary: Founded an important royal dynasty in 427 CE after earlier local settlement.

societies.name: Kaminaljuyu regional Maya-centre
societies.summary: Highland urban community influenced by exchange with Teotihuacan in the Classic period.

societies.name: El Mirador lowland Maya centre
societies.summary: Large preclassic settlement and monumental ceremonial landscape.

societies.name: Nakbe Preclassic Maya centre
societies.summary: Early monumental Maya lowland centre with complex preclassic urban growth.

societies.name: Izapa ceremonial community
societies.summary: Sculpture and ceremonial traditions at a regional interchange zone.

societies.name: Takalik Abaj ceremonial centre
societies.summary: Highland/Pacific centre with long-lived monument and exchange traditions.

societies.name: Hopewell ceremonial networks
societies.summary: Geometric earthworks, ceremonies and exchange links, not a single people or state.

societies.name: Havana Hopewell regional sites
societies.summary: Linked Eastern Woodland material and ceremonial traditions.

societies.name: Early Hohokam communities
societies.summary: Distinct irrigation and settlement traditions in southwest North America; not an empire.

societies.name: Early ancestral Puebloan communities
societies.summary: Southwestern farming and village traditions preceding later Pueblo settlements.

societies.name: Dorset Paleo-Inuit culture
societies.summary: Archaeological cultural tradition with specialised Arctic lifeways; exact regional phases differ.

societies.name: Old Bering Sea archaeological traditions
societies.summary: Marine hunting and walrus-ivory production traditions.

societies.name: Ipiutak archaeological culture
societies.summary: Distinctive ivory objects, dwellings and burial practices.

societies.name: Paracas cultures
societies.summary: Mortuary and extraordinary textile traditions predating Nasca.

societies.name: Chavin religious-material traditions
societies.summary: Pan-regional ceremonial imagery and monuments; not a modern territorial state.

societies.name: Nasca cultural traditions
societies.summary: Pottery, textile and landscape geoglyph traditions linked to diverse regional centres.

societies.name: Moche polities and cultures
societies.summary: Powerful valley-level centres with monumental adobe architecture and specialised craft.

societies.name: Pukara / early Titicaca basin cultures
societies.summary: Highland civic and artistic traditions preceding later Tiwanaku apogee.

societies.name: Tiwanaku early settlement and later polity
societies.summary: Pre-500 ritual and urban growth preceded peak political influence during following centuries.

societies.name: Recuay cultural traditions
societies.summary: Ceramic and mortuary developments in Peru north-central highlands.

societies.name: Huarpa communities
societies.summary: Earlier regional social and agricultural systems in the later Wari heartland.

societies.name: Emerging Wari cultural and political centres
societies.summary: Wari development begins near end of research window; major expansion belongs later period.

societies.name: Gallinazo / Viru Valley culture
societies.summary: Early urban and ceremonial communities including Gallinazo complex.

societies.name: Jama-Coaque regional traditions
societies.summary: Distinctive ceramics and settlement patterns in northern Andean coastal region.

societies.name: La Tolita-Tumaco traditions
societies.summary: Ceramic and metallurgical traditions; regional limits and dating require targeted archaeology.

societies.name: Early Saladoid ceramic traditions
societies.summary: Ceramic and settlement traditions linked to early Caribbean island networks.

societies.name: Western Polynesian island communities
societies.summary: Long-established western Polynesian communities with distinct voyaging traditions.

societies.name: Mangaasi-related archaeological tradition
societies.summary: Island ceramic and settlement period classifications vary by site.

societies.name: Sohano archaeological tradition
societies.summary: Material-culture tradition in a region of long-established Melanesian settlement.

societies.name: Early Caroline Islands island communities
societies.summary: Early settlement chronology uncertain and requires island-specific radiocarbon verification.

societies.name: New Guinea Highlands agricultural communities
societies.summary: Long histories of land management and agriculture; one name does not denote a uniform society.

societies.name: Arnhem Land rock art traditions
societies.summary: Archaeologically long-lived painting traditions; no fixed single tradition or date of origin.

societies.name: Gunditjmara Budj Bim cultural landscape
societies.summary: Multi-millennial aquaculture landscape; a precise 500 BCE-500 CE construction year is not established.

societies.name: Aboriginal Australian peoples (regional diversity overview)
societies.summary: Meta-record for exploring regional archaeological case studies only; never render as a single political marker.

societies.name: Torres Strait Islander antecedent communities
societies.summary: Archaeological traditions are site-specific; do not project modern language or territorial boundaries backwards.

societies.name: Chu state in Warring States China
societies.summary: Major regional court conquered during Qin unification.

societies.name: Qi state in Warring States China
societies.summary: Eastern Warring States polity conquered in the last phase of Qin unification.

societies.name: Zhao state in Warring States China
societies.summary: One of the major late Zhou competitors whose political centre was absorbed by Qin.

events.title: Athenian Cleisthenic reforms
events.summary: Civic reforms traditionally dated 508/507 BCE underlie Athenian political institutions but did not grant universal citizenship.

events.title: Ionian revolt against Achaemenid control
events.summary: Greek-speaking Ionian settlements rebel against Persian imperial authority; later commemorations shaped Greek-Persian narratives.

events.title: Battle of Marathon
events.summary: Athenian and allied soldiers repulse an Achaemenid expedition near Marathon.

events.title: Persian campaigns and Greek coalition resistance
events.summary: Xerxes campaigns in Greece; Salamis and Plataea are pivotal episodes within larger wars.

events.title: Growth of early Buddhist and Jain traditions
events.summary: Religious and philosophical communities develop in northeastern South Asia; exact lifetime dates for early teachers remain debated.

events.title: Formation of Delian League
events.summary: Greek maritime alliance later evolves into coercive Athenian predominance.

events.title: Peloponnesian War
events.summary: Prolonged war between Athenian and Spartan coalitions reshapes Greek politics.

events.title: Battle of Leuctra
events.summary: Theban victory weakens Spartan hegemony.

events.title: Battle of Chaeronea
events.summary: Philip II establishes Macedonian hegemony after victory over a Greek coalition.

events.title: Alexander's conquests of Achaemenid core
events.summary: Macedonian campaigns culminate in the overthrow of Achaemenid rule; a multi-year process not a single battle.

events.title: Death of Alexander and successor struggles
events.summary: Alexander dies in Babylon; successors compete for power across the conquered territories.

events.title: Emergence of the Maurya Empire
events.summary: Chandragupta's regime replaces the Nandas in Magadha in the late fourth century BCE; dates are conventional.

events.title: Seleucid dynastic foundation
events.summary: Seleucus I establishes a major Hellenistic successor monarchy in western Asia.

events.title: Ptolemy I assumes kingship in Egypt
events.summary: Start of the Ptolemaic royal dynasty in Hellenistic Egypt.

events.title: Seleucid-Mauryan settlement
events.summary: Relations between Seleucus I and Chandragupta involve territorial and diplomatic arrangements; details rely partly on later sources.

events.title: First Punic War
events.summary: Rome and Carthage fight for western Mediterranean influence, especially Sicily.

events.title: Ashoka's edicts and imperial moral policy
events.summary: Rock and pillar inscriptions from Ashoka's reign document governance, religious ethics and international referents.

events.title: Arsacid Parthian dynastic formation
events.summary: Arsacid state formation begins as Seleucid authority changes in the Iranian east.

events.title: Qin unification of Warring States
events.summary: Qin ruler Zheng conquers rival major states and assumes imperial title.

events.title: Second Punic War
events.summary: Hannibal campaigns in Italy; war extends across western Mediterranean and ends in Roman victory.

events.title: Battle of Zama
events.summary: Scipio and allied Numidian forces defeat Hannibal in North Africa.

events.title: Han imperial dynasty begins
events.summary: Liu Bang establishes Han dynasty after Qin collapse and civil conflict.

events.title: Masinissa's reign and Numidian consolidation
events.summary: Under Masinissa, Numidian royal patronage encourages farming and urbanism; not a uniformly urban kingdom.

events.title: Shunga dynasty succeeds Mauryan state in Magadha
events.summary: Political transition in northern India as Mauryan imperial cohesion ends.

events.title: Han silk cartography at Mawangdui
events.summary: Silk topographic and garrison maps were buried by 168 BCE; production date of each map differs.

events.title: Zhang Qian's Western Regions diplomatic mission
events.summary: Han diplomatic mission expanded literate Chinese geographical knowledge of Central Asia; not an instant inauguration of all Eurasian trade.

events.title: Pergamon bequest provides Rome an Asian province
events.summary: Territorial and political expansion of Roman rule into western Anatolia.

events.title: Later Zhang Qian missions under Emperor Wu
events.summary: Second diplomatic mission promoted ties with Central Asian populations.

events.title: Han campaigns against Dayuan
events.summary: Chinese expeditions westward demonstrate competition over horses, diplomacy and frontier authority.

events.title: Social War and extension of Roman citizenship
events.summary: Italian allies' revolt leads toward broader Roman citizenship rights on the peninsula.

events.title: Spartacus-led slave revolt
events.summary: Enslaved labourers and others resist Roman military authority in Italy.

events.title: Parthian defeat of Crassus at Carrhae
events.summary: Parthian forces defeat Roman invasion; trade connections coexist with intense imperial rivalry.

events.title: Caesar crosses Rubicon
events.summary: Caesar's challenge escalates the political crisis of the late Roman Republic.

events.title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
events.summary: Senators kill Caesar amid republican institutional conflict.

events.title: Battle of Actium
events.summary: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra's coalition.

events.title: End of Ptolemaic Egypt and Roman annexation
events.summary: Roman rule replaces Ptolemaic monarchy; Egyptian cultures and social institutions continue.

events.title: Augustan constitutional settlement
events.summary: Conventional starting year for imperial Principate, not the creation of Roman culture.

events.title: Augustus makes Juba II client king of Mauretania
events.summary: Client kingship and cross-cultural scholarship persist within Roman diplomatic structures.

events.title: Periplus describes Red Sea-Africa-Arabia-India trade
events.summary: Greek-language merchant text records ports, seasonal winds and commodities; broad composition mid-first-century CE.

events.title: Claudius's invasion of southern Britain
events.summary: Roman military expansion begins a centuries-long provincial process, without erasure of local populations.

events.title: Direct Roman administration follows Mauretanian client monarchy
events.summary: Roman provinces replace local royal government in the western Maghreb.

events.title: First Jewish-Roman War
events.summary: Revolt against Roman authority in Judea; Jerusalem's temple destroyed in 70.

events.title: Vesuvius eruption buries Pompeii and Herculaneum
events.summary: Volcanic eruption preserves exceptional evidence for urban life, crafts and inequality in Roman Italy.

events.title: Rome annexes Nabataea as Arabia province
events.summary: Roman provincial governance replaces Nabataean kingship in northwestern Arabia.

events.title: Ban Zhao's Han historiographical scholarship
events.summary: Women in Han elite scholarly families could contribute to texts and court learning; attribution and exact dates need nuanced treatment.

events.title: Bar Kokhba revolt in Roman Judaea
events.summary: Major rebellion and severe Roman suppression with lasting impacts on regional communities.

events.title: Antonine plague spreads across Roman world
events.summary: Epidemic coincides with imperial military movement; diagnosis of pathogen remains debated.

events.title: Eastern Han ends and Three Kingdoms emerge
events.summary: Dynastic division involves rival courts and military regimes rather than the disappearance of Chinese society.

events.title: Ardashir establishes Sasanian rule
events.summary: Sasanian political dynasty displaces Arsacid imperial leadership in Iran.

events.title: Roman third-century political and military crises
events.summary: Repeated succession crises, warfare and regional breakaway regimes reshape imperial institutions.

events.title: Kushan-linked Buddhist art and patronage
events.summary: Buddhist image production and monastic patronage grow across Gandhara and neighbouring regions; diffuse dates.

events.title: Palmyra exercises regional imperial authority
events.summary: Palmyrene leadership develops an extensive but short-lived regional political system during Roman crisis.

events.title: Diocletian's reforms and tetrarchic experiment
events.summary: Imperial government reorganises taxation, military arrangements and ruling hierarchy.

events.title: Western Jin reunifies major Chinese states
events.summary: Jin rule ends Three Kingdoms competition for a period; later political fractures remain.

events.title: Kofun mound construction and regional Yamato consolidation
events.summary: Elaborate elite burial mounds reflect changing power and transregional contact; no single exact start year.

events.title: Aksumite royal coinage attested
events.summary: Minting documents Aksum's political power and participation in Red Sea commercial systems.

events.title: Constantine wins Battle of Milvian Bridge
events.summary: One stage in Constantine's pursuit of control over Roman government.

events.title: Constantine and Licinius grant Christian toleration
events.summary: Religious policy changes amid a still religiously diverse Roman world; not a universal instant Christianisation.

events.title: Goguryeo takes Lelang commandery
events.summary: Termination of a Chinese-commandery institution centuries after Han dynasty itself had ended; avoid literal active Han participant label.

events.title: Constantinople established as imperial centre
events.summary: Site of Byzantium becomes New Rome and major seat of continuing Eastern Roman government.

events.title: Ezana-era royal adoption of Christianity
events.summary: Christian iconography and inscriptions support fourth-century court religious change; date approximate.

events.title: Goguryeo court receives Buddhism
events.summary: Conventional court-adoption milestone within wider east Asian Buddhist circulation.

events.title: Battle of Adrianople
events.summary: Roman army defeated by Gothic coalition and Emperor Valens killed.

events.title: Teotihuacan-linked arrival at Tikal
events.summary: Tikal inscriptions mark a political transition involving Teotihuacan-related actors; interpretation of conquest remains debated.

events.title: Transmission of Sue stoneware production to Japan
events.summary: Late fourth to fifth century pottery practices spread via Korean peninsula links and immigrant artisans.

events.title: Division of Roman imperial courts after Theodosius I
events.summary: Durable western and eastern courts emerge, but Roman institutional continuity remains.

events.title: Sack of Rome by Alaric's forces
events.summary: Symbolic sack of city while Western Roman government continues.

events.title: Royal dynastic foundation at Copan
events.summary: Dynastic chronology founded by K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' in 427 CE; city and Maya culture predate this reign.

events.title: Vandals establish kingdom in former Roman Africa

connections.summary: Qin unified major Chinese states in 221 BCE, three years before the Second Punic War began in the western Mediterranean in 218 BCE; both belong to the closing decades of the third century BCE.

connections.title: Three distinct worlds around 100 CE
connections.summary: Roman Red Sea commerce and Kushan South Asia coexisted with Teotihuacan urban growth and Hopewell exchange in North America.
connections.comparison_caveat: Trade connection only within parts of Afro-Eurasia

connections.title: Fall of Carthage and changing Han empire
connections.summary: The Roman destruction of Carthage in 146 BCE occurred within the long Western Han era, but the latter polity had begun in 206 BCE. The two developments are not assumed to have been directly connected.
connections.comparison_caveat: Han foundation precedes Carthage by sixty years; comparison is contemporary state context, not simultaneous event timing.

connections.region: Europe, West Asia and South Asia
connections.title: Macedonian succession and Mauryan formation
connections.summary: Alexander died as the Hellenistic successor order emerged and Mauryan power was developing in the Ganges basin.

connections.title: Parallel information networks in the first century CE
connections.summary: In the first century CE, Red Sea maritime commerce described by the Periplus coexisted with the continuing Eastern Han administrative record tradition; neither source proves direct permanent Rome-Han diplomacy.
connections.comparison_caveat: One named event plus contemporaneous Han contextual culture; explicitly not a direct-contact claim.

connections.title: Ashoka's inscriptions and Hellenistic kingdoms
connections.summary: Ashokan royal edicts were produced while Hellenistic successor states operated around the eastern Mediterranean.
connections.comparison_caveat: Some inscriptions refer to western Hellenistic rulers; exact identification can be debated

connections.title: Moche landscapes and emerging Kofun Japan
connections.summary: North-coastal Andean monumental centres flourished while elite burial mounds expanded in Japan.

connections.title: Copán dynasty and Roman imperial change
connections.summary: Copán royal inscriptions date a dynastic foundation to 427, while Roman courts had separated east and west.

connections.title: 476 was not the end of the world
connections.summary: Western Roman imperial office ended in 476, one year after Goguryeo's important 475 capture of a Baekje capital.

connections.title: Independent craft traditions
connections.summary: Dong Son bronze objects were part of Southeast Asian material traditions during centuries when Hellenistic dynasties reorganised Mediterranean and western Asian politics. No direct contact is inferred.
connections.comparison_caveat: Broad comparative observation; no specific contact inferred

research_gaps.description: Regional languages, early iron-working and agriculture cannot be reduced to one pan-Bantu cultural or political actor.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Research regional dated archaeological sequences and provenance-led entities.

research_gaps.description: Urban influence zones are not surveyed empire borders; unqualified hard polygons would mislead.

research_gaps.description: Moche, Nazca, Recuay and early Tiwanaku labels span distinct cultural and political units; exact dynastic state claims are often unwarranted.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Link site-level excavation and settlement histories.

research_gaps.description: Saladoid and other island archaeology requires regional sequence and migration nuance.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Review dated Caribbean ceramics and regional island settlement studies.

research_gaps.description: Most named political actors before late Classic Maya inscriptions are archaeologically anonymous; do not manufacture leaders.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Use inscription databases and explicitly anonymous actors.

research_gaps.description: Han, Western Han, Eastern Han and Xin are separate political phases, not four unrelated civilisations.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Use shared identity graph with subordinate period entities.

research_gaps.description: Traditional early Three Kingdoms foundation years are not precise archaeological state-formation years.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Cross-reference specialist Korean archaeology against later dynastic traditions.

research_gaps.description: Funan and related first-millennium polity labels mostly arise from later external textual accounts.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Distinguish excavated sites from historiographical political labels.

research_gaps.description: Remote East Polynesia should not be backdated into first millennium BCE or first five centuries CE from superseded older museum summaries.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Use radiocarbon-reviewed settlement ranges; reject unsupported early dates.

research_gaps.description: Modern language maps do not establish boundaries in ancient centuries; living knowledge has cultural protocols.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Consult region-specific archaeology and Traditional Owner governance before detailed map layers.

research_gaps.description: Torres Strait communities need archaeological dating and island-specific historical accounts.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Collect specialist Queensland and New Guinea archaeology and community sources.

research_gaps.description: Itiner-e shows most mapped Roman road lengths conjectural, not certain.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Preserve segment confidence in any optional route overlay.

research_gaps.description: 476 ended western imperial office not eastern Roman state; avoid disappearance of Roman culture and institutions.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Model separate western office and continuing eastern polity.

research_gaps.description: Many entity seeds have one institution-wide chronology source; not independently corroborated.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Perform claim-by-claim specialist source audit; preserve verification status.

research_gaps.description: Catalogued historical maps do not entail permission to reproduce photographs or collection scans.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Check image rights and copy metadata at item level; never distribute unchecked images.

research_gaps.description: Political and cultural dates often conventional, particularly BCE; year 500 CE overlaps the next period's earlier pack.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Use uncertainty bounds, stable IDs and a single canonical owner for 500 CE on import.

research_gaps.description: Oldest surviving evidence is not invention; paper, glassblowing and iron need separate invention/adoption/diffusion claims.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Attach archaeological context and distinguish dated statuses in technology graph.

research_gaps.description: Ancient population figures for cities and empires have extreme model uncertainty.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Collect methodology, ranges and source debate rather than fixed point estimates.

research_gaps.description: Elite texts and tombs overrepresent rulers, soldiers and literate households.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Expand craft, diet, gender, rural labour and household archaeology.

research_gaps.description: Buddha, Mahavira and several teachers have disputed lifetimes and hagiographic traditions.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Model alternative chronologies rather than exact birth dates.

research_gaps.description: Indirectly traded objects do not prove full geographic awareness of a network.
research_gaps.recommended_next_step: Apply attested / inference / unknown evidence layers by society and date.
